title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: governance policies check outgoing emails before they are sent
summary: Hold: the policy automation row presents a record-creation endpoint as the way to configure content checks and enforcement strictness, which its reference does not document. The roadmap facts, prerequisites and main product behaviour are supported; the page also correctly highlights Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of whether a sender can override a block.

claims.fix: Include the intervening dialog heading in the structured and rendered path: Service > Governance > New policy > Add a policy > Content to check > How strictly to enforce.

claims.claim: POST /msdyn_guardrail_rules configures which policies exist, what they check and how strictly they enforce.
claims.quote: Create ... POST /msdyn_guardrail_rules ... msdyn_active_versionid: Look up fetching specific version of guardrail rule
claims.fix: Narrow controls[1].governs and its rendered label to 'Creation of governance policy records'. Replace its note with 'The request body sets msdyn_name to name the new policy record. This Create operation does not document configuring content checks or enforcement strictness; use the documented UI for those settings.' Keep POST /msdyn_guardrail_rules and its existing reference URL. Do not present creation of the policy record as automation for its content checks and enforcement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Replacing the default Send button with a custom command stops built-in governance validation from running automatically.
claims.quote: If you replace the default Send button with a custom command, the built-in governance validation doesn't run automatically before an email is sent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom Send code must call validateForSend before sending to integrate governance validation.
claims.quote: Always call validateForSend from your custom command before sending the email.

claims.claim: A customized Customer Service workspace app may need its Governance site-map entry manually added using Power Apps.
claims.quote: When you're using a customized Customer Service workspace app, the Governance option might not appear in the site map. You need to manually add the Governance entry to the site map by using the Power Apps designer.

claims.claim: The Governance site-map entry instructions grant Write on msdyn_guardrail_rule.
claims.quote: After you create the page, open the right-side panel and add the following table privileges: ... Table: msdyn_guardrail_rule ... Permission: Write

claims.claim: The configuration guide does not explicitly say that its UI toggle writes msdyn_isenabled.
claims.quote: Searched: "msdyn_isenabled" "governance" toggle. Opened Configure governance policies and the msdyn_governanceagent_status reference: the guide gives the toggle and the reference describes the enabled property, but neither explicitly maps the UI write.

claims.claim: The cited rule reference does not map a column to the UI enforcement or Policy strictness settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "msdyn_guardrail_rule_version" enforcement strictness. Read writable columns in msdyn_guardrail_rule and msdyn_guardrail_rule_version: the latter documents an LLM decision threshold, but neither maps the named UI settings to columns.

claims.claim: The policy evaluation underlying strictness uses AI judgement rather than only a deterministic rule match.
claims.quote: Score threshold for violation determination. LLM score less than threshold equals violated, score greater than or equal to threshold equals pass.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/msdyn_guardrail_rule_version to sources as support for the AI-judgement statement.

claims.claim: The custom Send documentation says a user can override a block and send the email.
claims.quote: Block the email and display a dialog that explains which policies are violated. The user can override the restriction and send the email, or cancel.

claims.claim: The custom Send documentation says a block override is recorded.
claims.quote: The override is recorded.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, notification bullet
claims.claim: The checklist attributes notification of both representatives and customers to Microsoft's requirements.
claims.quote: customers must adequately notify users ... In addition, customers are encouraged to have a mechanism in place to inform their service representatives
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'Agree with legal and HR how users are notified that communications may be monitored, as Microsoft requires; Microsoft also encourages informing service representatives.' Microsoft requires user notification but only encourages representative notification.

claims.claim: All controls the governance checklist tells readers to configure or check are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Confirm the CSR Manager role holders ... Set up Microsoft Copilot credits ... provide consent ... enable AI agents ... Check every custom Send command ... The table contains only governance enablement and policy authoring.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps for security roles/table privileges, Copilot credits setup, cross-region consent and AI-agent enablement, and the At rollout custom Send validation step have no corresponding control rows. Keep these as prerequisite or developer notes rather than table-backed configuration checklist steps; do not add rows as part of this correction.
